name: Nabota

lead: Nabota is a botulinum toxin type A from Daewoong of South Korea, sold in the US as Jeuveau. People use it to smooth frown lines and crow's feet, and it is also discussed for slimming the masseter muscle to narrow the lower face and for calf contouring.

It blocks acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, weakening the injected muscle temporarily so wrinkles soften or bulk reduces. It has been studied in glabellar and crow's feet lines, masseter hypertrophy, calf contouring, post-stroke spasticity and blepharospasm, including comparisons against Botox.

paras: A clinician injects the target muscles in a short visit, and people repeat treatments as the effect wears off over a few months. Wrinkle use is the established route; jaw slimming is an off-label use that tends to show over weeks as the muscle shrinks.

It is prescription-only and the effect is temporary. Reviews note that repeated exposure to any foreign protein can provoke immune responses and that evidence on the purity and immunogenicity of newer formulations is limited.

angle.text: Nabota, sold as Jeuveau in the US, smooths frown lines and is also used to slim the masseter for a narrower lower face. The toxin relaxes the targeted muscles so wrinkles soften and bulk reduces. Wrinkle use has trial support, while jaw slimming appears in smaller reports and is largely off-label.

lead: Nabota (prabotulinumtoxinA) is a botulinum toxin type A made by Daewoong Pharmaceutical of South Korea.[1][2] The same toxin is marketed in the US as Jeuveau, sold by Evolus and manufactured by Daewoong, according to Wikipedia.[3]
It has been studied in post-stroke spasticity, blepharospasm, glabellar and crow's feet lines, masseter hypertrophy and calf contouring, among others.[4][5][6][7][8]
Reviews note that evidence on the purity and immunogenicity of newer toxin formulations such as Nabota is limited.[1]

paras: Cosmetic uses studied include glabellar lines in a phase 4 single-arm study,[6] masseter reduction in a split-face comparison with Botox,[5] and calf contouring in a pilot comparison.[7] Medical uses studied include post-stroke upper limb spasticity, where a phase 3 trial randomized 197 patients to Nabota or Botox,[4] and cervical and shoulder myofascial pain in a pilot study.[8]

A 2020 review of neurotoxin impurities said Nabota/Jeuveau, Meditoxin/Neuronox and Botulax contain nontoxic accessory proteins and excipients, that any non-human protein can provoke immune reactions with repeated use, and that clinical evidence on purity and treatment failure is limited.[1] A 2018 comparison of formulations in Asia likewise said essential formulation data are not always public.[2]

Registered trials include a phase 2/3 study in crow's feet lines (n=238), a phase 3 study in benign masseteric hypertrophy (n=180), a phase 2/3 study in blepharospasm (n=234) and a phase 4 comparison with onabotulinumtoxinA for facial wrinkles (n=26).[9][10][11][12] The publications above report split-face, pilot and single-arm designs for cosmetic use.[5][6][7]
